papers.title: Reducing Fixed-Batch Client Idleness in Many-Client Edge Split Learning
authors: Mohammad Kohankhaki, Valentin Rentschler, Carsten Kamp, Sigrid Brell-Cokcan, Anke Schmeink
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2609.29395v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Parallel Split Learning with Global Sampling (GPSL) trains a split model on a fixed-size batch drawn from the data of all clients. When the client population is much larger than the batch, most clients contribute no data in a round, and additional server capacity does not change this. We propose Global Clustered Parallel Split Learning (GCPSL), which assigns clients to stable clusters, runs one GPSL workload per cluster concurrently, and periodically fuses the split-model replicas. We derive the expected direct data participation under the batch sampler, which separates repeated sampling of the same clients from idling at the fusion barrier.
